category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Contrast the immediate physiological response of GnRH Agonists (e.g., Leuprolide) versus GnRH Antagonists (e.g., Ganirelix) in prostate cancer treatment.
back:
• Agonists: Cause initial 'tumor flare' due to LH/testosterone surge.
• Antagonists: Produce immediate LH suppression without an initial surge.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: List the paradoxical adverse effects observed in men who consume excessive doses of anabolic steroids.
back:
• Feminization (gynecomastia) due to peripheral aromatization to estrogen.
• Testicular shrinkage and infertility via pituitary feedback inhibition.
• Possible cholestatic jaundice.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: The rare but serious central nervous system adverse effect of somatropin therapy in children is [___].
back:
• Pseudotumor cerebri (idiopathic intracranial hypertension)
• Presents with headache and papilledema
• Other childhood risks include slipped capital femoral epiphysis and progression of scoliosis.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: A 50-year-old male treated with Octreotide for acromegaly presents with right upper quadrant pain and fatty food intolerance. Identify the most likely pharmacological cause.
back:
• Biliary sludge or gallstones
• Mechanism: Inhibition of cholecystokinin release and reduced gallbladder contractility
• Occurs in up to 50% of patients on long-term therapy.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Detail the specific role of Human Chorionic Gonadotropin (hCG) in female ovulation induction protocols.
back:
• Acts as an LH receptor agonist
• Mimics the natural mid-cycle LH surge
• Triggers final oocyte maturation and facilitates ovulation after follicle priming with FSH.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Contrast the tissue-specific actions of Tamoxifen and Raloxifene on the uterine endometrium.
back:
• Tamoxifen: Partial agonist (increases risk of endometrial hyperplasia and cancer)
• Raloxifene: Estrogen antagonist (no increased risk of endometrial cancer)
• Both remain agonists in bone and antagonists in breast.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Enumerate the androgenic adverse effects observed in women using Danazol for endometriosis.
back:
• Acne and hirsutism
• Weight gain and edema
• Deepening of voice (irreversible)
• Decreased breast size and menstrual irregularities.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: The primary clinical danger of utilizing Diethylstilbestrol (DES) during pregnancy is the development of [___] in female offspring.
back:
• Clear cell vaginal adenocarcinoma
• Also associated with infertility and structural reproductive tract abnormalities
• Historically used to prevent miscarriages, now strictly contraindicated.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: A patient undergoing medical abortion with Mifepristone and Misoprostol presents with sudden-onset sepsis and hypotension without fever. Identify the associated pathogen.
back:
• Clostridium sordellii
• Rare but fatal infection associated with medical abortion
• Presents with profound leukocytosis and capillary leak syndrome.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Explain why Flutamide is co-administered during the first week of Leuprolide therapy in advanced prostate cancer.
back:
• Prevents 'Tumor Flare'
• Leuprolide initially causes a transient surge in LH and testosterone
• Flutamide blocks androgen receptors to prevent exacerbation of bone pain or urinary obstruction.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Distinguish between the primary metabolic glucose-related toxicities of Somatropin and Mecasermin.
back:
• Somatropin: Causes hyperglycemia (anti-insulin effect)
• Mecasermin: Causes hypoglycemia (IGF-1 has insulin-like activity)
• Pre-meal snacks are required for Mecasermin administration.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Identify the two primary hematological indications for Desmopressin (DDAVP) administration.
back:
• Mild Hemophilia A (Factor VIII deficiency)
• von Willebrand Disease (Type 1)
• Mechanism: Stimulates release of Factor VIII and vWF from endothelial storage sites.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: In the management of postpartum care, [___] is administered intravenously to control uterine hemorrhage by stimulating powerful contractions.
back: Oxytocin. Clinical uses: Induction/augmentation of labor and postpartum hemorrhage control. Adverse effects: Fetal distress, maternal water retention (ADH-like effect), and uterine rupture.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: A 30-year-old female with endometriosis is prescribed a drug that inhibits multiple cytochrome P450 enzymes and acts as a weak partial agonist of androgen receptors. This drug is [___].
back: Danazol. Clinical uses: Endometriosis and fibrocystic breast disease. Adverse effects: Weight gain, acne, hirsutism, menstrual disturbances, and hepatic dysfunction.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Explain the pharmacological mechanism and clinical utility of Mifepristone (RU 486) when combined with Misoprostol.
back: Mechanism: Competitively antagonizes progesterone and glucocorticoid receptors. Clinical Use: Medical abortion (up to 49 days) and postcoital contraception. Adverse effects: Vaginal bleeding and GI disturbances.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Contrast the intended clinical use and specific toxic profile of anabolic steroids (e.g., Oxandrolone) versus physiological testosterone replacement.
back: Uses: Anabolic steroids promote weight gain in wasting syndromes; Testosterone treats male hypogonadism. Toxicity: Anabolic steroids carry higher risks of cholestatic jaundice and hepatocellular carcinoma.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Identify the clinical application and primary adverse effect of Fulvestrant in oncology.
back: Clinical use: Advanced hormone-responsive breast cancer resistant to tamoxifen. Adverse effects: Hot flushes, headaches, and injection site reactions. It is a pure estrogen receptor antagonist in all tissues.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Beyond central diabetes insipidus, Desmopressin is used to manage mild Hemophilia A because it stimulates the release of [___].
back: Coagulation Factor VIII and von Willebrand factor. Mechanism: Extrarenal V2 receptor agonism. Clinical uses: Hemophilia A, vWD, and nocturnal enuresis. Toxicities: Hyponatremia and headache.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: A postmenopausal woman on unopposed estrogen therapy for hot flushes presents with vaginal bleeding. Explain the risk associated with this therapy and the pharmacological preventive measure.
back: Risk: Endometrial hyperplasia and carcinoma. Prevention: Co-administration of a progestin (e.g., Medroxyprogesterone) to stabilize the endometrium. Other risks: Thromboembolism and gallbladder disease.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Explain why Spironolactone is used in the management of female hirsutism despite being classified primarily as a diuretic.
back: Mechanism: Competitively inhibits androgen receptors and reduces steroid synthesis. Clinical use: Hirsutism and PCOS symptoms. Adverse effects: Hyperkalemia, gynecomastia, and menstrual irregularities.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Distinguish between older 19-nortestosterone progestins (e.g., Norgestrel) and newer analogs (e.g., Desogestrel) regarding their side effect profiles.
back: Androgenicity: Older progestins (Norgestrel) have higher androgenic activity (acne, hirsutism). Newer analogs (Desogestrel) are less androgenic but associated with slightly higher thromboembolic risks.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Describe the composition and primary clinical use of Menotropins (hMG) in fertility treatment.
back: Composition: Purified mixture of FSH and LH from postmenopausal urine. Use: Stimulation of follicle development in women and spermatogenesis in men. Adverse effects: Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: In pediatric patients receiving Somatropin for growth hormone deficiency, a rare but serious adverse effect involving increased intracranial pressure is [___].
back:
Pseudotumor cerebri. Key monitoring includes:
• Fundoscopy to check for papilledema.
• Assessment for persistent headaches or visual disturbances.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: A 55-year-old male with cirrhosis presents with acute hematemesis from esophageal varices. Which posterior pituitary hormone analog is administered for its V1-mediated vasoconstrictive properties to control this bleeding?
back:
Vasopressin.
• Mechanism: Activates V1 receptors on vascular smooth muscle.
• Use: Emergency management of esophageal variceal or colonic diverticular hemorrhage.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Describe the pharmacological mechanism by which Danazol treats endometriosis and its resulting androgenic adverse effects.
back:
• Mechanism: Weak partial agonist at progestin/androgen receptors; inhibits CYP450 enzymes involved in gonadal steroid synthesis.
• Side Effects: Acne, hirsutism, weight gain, and potential hepatic dysfunction.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Contrast the hepatic effects of oral ethinyl estradiol with those of transdermal estradiol patches regarding clotting factor synthesis.
back:
• Oral: High hepatic-to-peripheral ratio due to first-pass metabolism; significantly increases clotting factor synthesis.
• Transdermal: Bypasses first-pass liver exposure; minimizes stimulation of hepatic clotting factors, reducing thromboembolic risk.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Enumerate the non-contraceptive clinical benefits of using combined oral contraceptives (COCs) in young women.
back:
• Reduced risk of ovarian and endometrial cancers.
• Decreased incidence of iron deficiency anemia and dysmenorrhea.
• Lower risk of ovarian cysts and pelvic inflammatory disease (PID).

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: To prevent the specific adverse effect of [___] in children treated with Mecasermin (recombinant IGF-1), the drug must be administered shortly after a meal or snack.
back:
Hypoglycemia.
• IGF-1 possesses insulin-like effects on glucose metabolism.
• Proper caloric intake is required before administration to maintain euglycemia.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: A 25-year-old female presents with vaginal clear-cell adenocarcinoma. History reveals her mother took a nonsteroidal estrogen agonist during pregnancy to prevent miscarriage. Identify the drug.
back:
Diethylstilbestrol (DES).
• Teratogenicity: Causes vaginal adenocarcinoma, infertility, and uterine abnormalities in female offspring.
• Status: Clinically obsolete for pregnant women due to these risks.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Explain why Oxytocin administration for labor augmentation requires careful monitoring of fluid balance and uterine tone.
back:
• Uterine Risk: Overstimulation can lead to uterine rupture or fetal distress.
• Fluid Risk: High doses activate vasopressin-like receptors, causing water intoxication and fluid retention.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Distinguish between Menotropins (hMG) and Urofollitropin regarding their hormonal content and clinical source.
back:
• Menotropins: Extracted from postmenopausal urine; contains both FSH and LH activity.
• Urofollitropin: Purified from postmenopausal urine; contains FSH activity only.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: List the potential hepatotoxic adverse effects associated with the illicit use of high-dose anabolic steroids (e.g., Oxandrolone).
back:
• Cholestatic jaundice.
• Elevated serum liver enzymes (AST/ALT).
• Increased risk of hepatocellular carcinoma with long-term use.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: A serious but rare adverse effect of Somatropin therapy in children characterized by increased intracranial pressure and papilledema is [___].
back:
• Pseudotumor cerebri
• Monitoring required: Frequent fundoscopic exams
• Management: Typically reversible upon discontinuation of growth hormone therapy.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: A 50-year-old male with acromegaly and a history of cholelithiasis requires pharmacological suppression of GH. Explain why somatostatin analogs like Octreotide may be problematic in this patient.
back:
• MOA: Inhibits cholecystokinin (CCK) release and gallbladder contractility
• Adverse Effect: Formation of biliary sludge and gallstones (up to 50% of patients)
• Other effects: Bradycardia and GI disturbances (steatorrhea).

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Identify the specific physiological role of Human Chorionic Gonadotropin (hCG) when used in female ovulation induction protocols.
back:
• LH Receptor Agonist: Mimics the natural mid-cycle LH surge
• Function: Triggers final oocyte maturation and ovulation
• Clinical Use: Administered after follicle development has been stimulated by FSH.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Contrast the effects of Tamoxifen and Raloxifene on endometrial tissue and the resulting clinical implications.
back:
• Tamoxifen: Estrogen agonist in endometrium; increases risk of endometrial hyperplasia/cancer
• Raloxifene: Estrogen antagonist in endometrium; no increased cancer risk
• Commonality: Both are antagonists in breast and agonists in bone.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Enumerate the clinical uses of Danazol and specify its primary enzymatic interference.
back:
• Uses: Endometriosis and fibrocystic breast disease
• Enzymatic MOA: Weak cytochrome P450 inhibitor (inhibits multiple steroidogenic enzymes)
• Side Effects: Weight gain, acne, and hirsutism due to weak androgenic activity.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: The gonadotropin preparation purified specifically from the urine of postmenopausal women, containing both FSH and LH activity, is [___].
back:
• Menotropins (hMG)
• Use: Stimulates follicle development in women and spermatogenesis in men
• Risk: Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS) and multiple pregnancies.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: A 38-year-old female who smokes one pack of cigarettes daily requests contraception. Justify why combined oral contraceptives (COCs) are generally avoided in this patient.
back:
• Thromboembolism Risk: Estrogen increases hepatic synthesis of clotting factors (VII, X, and fibrinogen)
• Synergistic Danger: Smoking plus age >35 significantly increases risk of MI and stroke
• Alternative: Progestin-only pills or IUD.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Discuss the clinical utility of Spironolactone in the management of female endocrine disorders despite its primary use as a diuretic.
back:
• Indication: Treatment of hirsutism in women
• MOA: Competitively inhibits androgen receptors and reduces 17-hydroxylase activity
• Common side effect: Menstrual irregularities and hyperkalemia.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Distinguish the extrarenal V2 receptor-mediated clinical application of Desmopressin from its use in diabetes insipidus.
back:
• Application: Mild Hemophilia A and von Willebrand disease (Type 1)
• Mechanism: Stimulates release of Factor VIII and von Willebrand factor from endothelial storage
• Advantage: Selective V2 action avoids V1-mediated vasoconstriction.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Identify the rare but life-threatening infectious complication specifically associated with the use of Mifepristone and Misoprostol for medical abortion.
back:
• Condition: Sepsis due to Clostridium sordellii
• Presentation: Absence of fever, but rapid progression to shock
• General side effects: Nausea, vomiting, and heavy vaginal bleeding.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: To prevent the primary adverse effect of the IGF-1 agonist Mecasermin, patients are advised to consume a snack or meal shortly before administration to avoid [___].
back:
- Hypoglycemia (most common toxicity)
- Intracranial hypertension
- Elevated liver enzymes

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: A pregnant woman undergoing labor induction with high-dose intravenous Oxytocin suddenly develops headache, confusion, and hyponatremia. Identify the likely mechanism.
back:
- Activation of vasopressin receptors by oxytocin at high doses
- Leads to excessive water retention (water intoxication)
- Risk of seizures or coma

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Explain why Menotropins (hMG) are specifically purified from the urine of postmenopausal women for use in infertility treatment.
back:
- Postmenopausal women have high FSH and LH levels due to lack of ovarian feedback
- hMG contains both FSH and LH activity
- Used to stimulate follicle development or spermatogenesis

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Contrast Urofollitropin with Follitropin alpha regarding their production source and pharmacological purity.
back:
- Urofollitropin: Purified human FSH extracted from postmenopausal urine
- Follitropin alpha: Recombinant human FSH produced in cell culture
- Follitropin is more consistent and potent

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Identify the high-yield long-term risks associated with the female offspring of women treated with Diethylstilbestrol (DES) during pregnancy.
back:
- Vaginal clear cell adenocarcinoma
- Infertility
- Ectopic pregnancy risk
- Structural uterine abnormalities

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: The non-FDA approved oxytocin receptor antagonist used in some countries as a tocolytic to suppress preterm labor is [___].
back:
- Atosiban
- Acts as a competitive antagonist
- Administered via IV infusion

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: A 24-year-old female with PCOS and hirsutism is prescribed Spironolactone. Explain the dual mechanism by which this drug reduces unwanted hair growth.
back:
- Competitive inhibition of androgen receptors
- Inhibition of steroid synthesis (CYP450 enzymes)
- Also acts as a potassium-sparing diuretic

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Describe the pharmacological strategy for using Human Chorionic Gonadotropin (hCG) in controlled ovulation induction protocols.
back:
- Administered as the final step after follicle maturation
- Acts as an LH analog (identical receptor binding)
- Triggers final oocyte maturation and ovulation

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Contrast the primary contraceptive mechanism of Combined Oral Contraceptives (COCs) with that of Progestin-only preparations.
back:
- COCs: Consistently inhibit ovulation via LH/FSH suppression
- Progestin-only: Primarily thickens cervical mucus and thins endometrium
- Ovulation is not always suppressed in progestin-only users

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Mention the specific biochemical mechanism by which Ketoconazole serves as a second-line therapy for advanced prostate cancer.
back:
- Non-selective inhibition of CYP450 enzymes
- Blocks both adrenal and gonadal steroid synthesis
- Dramatically reduces testosterone levels

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: In children with growth failure unresponsive to Somatropin due to growth hormone receptor mutations (Laron dwarfism), the primary therapeutic agent is [___].
back:
Mecasermin (recombinant IGF-1).
- Clinical Use: IGF-1 deficiency unresponsive to GH.
- Adverse Effects: Hypoglycemia (most common), intracranial hypertension, and asymptomatic elevation of liver enzymes.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: A 50-year-old male treated with Octreotide for acromegaly presents with right upper quadrant pain and fatty stools. Explain the underlying pharmacologic cause of these symptoms.
back:
Biliary complications (gallstones).
- Mechanism: Inhibition of cholecystokinin (CCK) release leads to reduced gallbladder contractility.
- Other Effects: GI distress (steatorrhea, nausea) and cardiac conduction abnormalities (bradycardia).

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
coreConcept: Oxytocin clinical use and fluid toxicity
front: Describe the clinical indications for intravenous Oxytocin and the major risk associated with its antidiuretic properties at high doses.
back:
Indications: Induction/augmentation of labor and control of postpartum hemorrhage.
- Risk: Water intoxication (hyponatremia).
- Other Risks: Uterine rupture, fetal distress, and placental abruption.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
coreConcept: V1 vs V2 receptor clinical targeting
front: Contrast the use of Desmopressin versus Vasopressin in the management of bleeding disorders and hemodynamic emergencies.
back:
Desmopressin (V2 selective): Used in Hemophilia A and von Willebrand disease to release Factor VIII/vWF.
- Vasopressin (Non-selective): Used for V1-mediated vasoconstriction in bleeding esophageal varices.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: List three high-yield non-contraceptive benefits of using combined hormonal oral contraceptives (COCs).
back:
- Reduced risk of endometrial and ovarian cancers.
- Decreased incidence of ovarian cysts and pelvic inflammatory disease (PID).
- Management of acne, hirsutism, and dysmenorrhea.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: A 26-year-old female treated for endometriosis presents with weight gain, deepened voice, and acne. These virilizing side effects are most likely caused by [___].
back:
Danazol.
- Mechanism: Weak partial agonist of androgen/progestin receptors; inhibits multiple P450 enzymes.
- Adverse Effects: Hirsutism, hepatic dysfunction, and menstrual disturbances.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: A woman using Mifepristone and Misoprostol for medical abortion presents with persistent fever and malaise. Identify a rare but lethal complication associated with this regimen.
back:
Sepsis due to unusual infections (e.g., Clostridium sordellii).
- Clinical Presentation: Sepsis without typical fever.
- Mechanism: Mifepristone blocks progesterone and glucocorticoid receptors, potentially altering the immune response.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Explain why chronic use of high-dose anabolic steroids like Oxandrolone results in testicular atrophy and gynecomastia in male athletes.
back:
- Testicular Atrophy: Feedback inhibition of LH/FSH secretion from the anterior pituitary.
- Gynecomastia: Excess exogenous androgens are peripherally converted (aromatized) into estrogens.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Distinguish between the mechanisms of Anastrozole and Fulvestrant in treating tamoxifen-resistant breast cancer.
back:
- Anastrozole: Aromatase inhibitor; prevents the final step of estrogen synthesis from androgens.
- Fulvestrant: Pure estrogen receptor (ER) antagonist; causes ER degradation in all tissues.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Enumerate the major metabolic and hepatic toxicities associated with high-dose estrogen therapy in postmenopausal women.
back:
- Hypertriglyceridemia (increased plasma triglycerides).
- Gallbladder disease (increased cholesterol in bile).
- Thromboembolism (increased synthesis of clotting factors in the liver).

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: In children with growth failure who are unresponsive to Growth Hormone due to GH receptor mutations, the recombinant IGF-1 analog used for treatment is [___].
back:
Mecasermin
- Clinical Use: Laron dwarfism (GH insensitivity) or IGF-1 deficiency.
- Adverse Effects: Hypoglycemia (primary) and intracranial hypertension.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: A 28-year-old female presents with milky nipple discharge and secondary amenorrhea. MRI confirms a microadenoma. Identify the first-line pharmacological agent and its most common cardiovascular adverse effect.
back:
Bromocriptine (or Cabergoline)
- Clinical Use: Hyperprolactinemia and Parkinson's disease.
- Adverse Effects: Orthostatic hypotension (common initial dose effect) and nausea.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Detail the physiological mechanism of Oxytocin in the management of post-partum hemorrhage.
back:
- Mechanism: Activates G-protein coupled receptors to increase intracellular calcium in uterine smooth muscle.
- Clinical Use: Induces rhythmic uterine contractions to compress spiral arteries and reduce bleeding.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Distinguish between Menotropins (hMG) and Urofollitropin regarding their hormonal composition and source.
back:
- Menotropins: Purified from postmenopausal urine; contains both FSH and LH activity.
- Urofollitropin: Purified from postmenopausal urine; contains FSH activity only.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Explain why Anastrozole is preferred over Tamoxifen in certain postmenopausal breast cancer patients, specifically regarding its enzymatic target.
back:
- Target: Nonsteroidal competitive inhibitor of Aromatase.
- Clinical Use: ER-positive breast cancer.
- Benefit: Avoids the risk of endometrial cancer associated with SERMs.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Long-term use of high-dose anabolic steroids like Oxandrolone is clinically associated with a specific hepatic complication called [___].
back:
Cholestatic Jaundice
- Other Adverse Effects: Peliosis hepatis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and decreased HDL levels.
- Clinical Use: Promoting weight gain in HIV/wasting syndromes.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: A 32-year-old female with endometriosis is treated with a drug that acts as a weak partial agonist of androgen receptors. Name the drug and its primary cutaneous adverse effect.
back:
Danazol
- Mechanism: Inhibits P450 enzymes and suppresses the pituitary-ovarian axis.
- Adverse Effects: Hirsutism, acne, and weight gain (androgenic effects).

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: In the context of preventing preterm labor, how does the mechanism of Atosiban differ from traditional beta-2 agonists?
back:
- Atosiban: Competitive antagonist of the Oxytocin receptor.
- Clinical Use: Tocolysis to delay delivery.
- Advantage: Lower incidence of maternal tachycardia compared to Terbutaline.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Contrast the hepatic impact of oral Ethinyl Estradiol versus transdermal Estradiol patches in hormone replacement therapy.
back:
- Oral: High hepatic-to-peripheral ratio due to first-pass metabolism; increases clotting factor synthesis.
- Transdermal: Bypasses first-pass effect; significantly lower risk of thromboembolism.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: List the rationale for using Ketoconazole in the management of advanced, hormone-resistant prostate cancer.
back:
- Mechanism: Non-selective inhibitor of cytochrome P450 enzymes (17,20-lyase).
- Effect: Suppresses both adrenal and gonadal androgen synthesis.
- Adverse Effects: Gynecomastia and hepatotoxicity.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: A rare but serious neurological adverse effect of Somatropin therapy in children is [___], which presents with headache, visual changes, and papilledema.
back:
• Pseudotumor cerebri (idiopathic intracranial hypertension).
• Other pediatric toxicities include slipped capital femoral epiphysis and progression of scoliosis.
• Requires regular monitoring of intracranial pressure symptoms.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: A 5-year-old child with growth failure unresponsive to GH therapy is diagnosed with a GH-receptor mutation. The drug prescribed must be taken shortly after a meal to prevent [___].
back:
• Hypoglycemia.
• Drug: Mecasermin (recombinant IGF-1).
• Indicated for Laron dwarfism (GH insensitivity) where IGF-1 production is impaired despite normal GH levels.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Explain the role of Desmopressin (DDAVP) in managing mild Hemophilia A or Type 1 von Willebrand disease.
back:
• Activates extrarenal V2 receptors.
• Stimulates release of Factor VIII and von Willebrand factor from endothelial cells.
• Used for minor surgery or bleeding control.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Contrast the gonadotropin content and clinical origin of Menotropins (hMG) with Urofollitropin.
back:
• Origin: Both extracted from postmenopausal urine.
• Menotropins: Contains a mixture of both FSH and LH activity.
• Urofollitropin: Purified preparation containing only FSH activity.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Identify the clinical applications of Danazol and its characteristic androgenic adverse effects.
back:
• Uses: Endometriosis and fibrocystic breast disease.
• Adverse Effects: Weight gain, acne, hirsutism, and deepening of voice.
• Mechanism: Weak partial agonist at androgen/progestin receptors.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: To prevent [___] following delivery, high-dose intravenous Oxytocin is routinely administered to ensure sustained uterine contraction.
back:
• Postpartum hemorrhage (uterine hemorrhage).
• Acts on G-protein coupled receptors to stimulate upper uterine segment contraction.
• Also used for labor induction.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: A woman using combined oral contraceptives is prescribed Rifampin. Explain the risk regarding contraceptive efficacy.
back:
• Increased risk of unintended pregnancy.
• Mechanism: Rifampin induces CYP3A4 enzymes.
• Result: Accelerated metabolism of estrogen/progestin reduces their serum concentration.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Describe the biochemical pathway by which excessive anabolic steroid use causes feminization (gynecomastia) in males.
back:
• Aromatization: Excess exogenous androgens are converted to estrogens in peripheral tissues.
• Negative Feedback: Suppresses LH, causing testicular atrophy and decreased endogenous testosterone.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Distinguish between the Progestin-only emergency contraceptive and the Yuzpe regimen regarding side effect profiles.
back:
• Progestin-only: L-norgestrel; significantly lower incidence of nausea and vomiting.
• Yuzpe Regimen: Combined estrogen-progestin; associated with high-dose estrogen-induced nausea.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Specify the primary physiological reason for limiting continuous GnRH agonist therapy (e.g., Leuprolide) to less than six months.
back:
• Avoidance of significant bone mineral density loss (osteoporosis).
• Caused by profound hypoestrogenism during sustained pituitary suppression.
• Can cause menopausal symptoms (hot flushes).

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Growth failure in children due to inactivating growth hormone (GH) receptor mutations is treated with [___], a recombinant form of insulin-like growth factor-1.
back:
Mecasermin. 
- **Clinical Use:** IGF-1 deficiency unresponsive to GH therapy.
- **Adverse Effects:** Hypoglycemia (primary) and intracranial hypertension. 
- **Prevention:** Consuming a meal shortly before administration.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: A 32-year-old female undergoing labor induction with a hormonal infusion develops sudden uterine hypertonus and fetal bradycardia. Identify the likely drug and its most dangerous maternal complication.
back:
Oxytocin. 
- **Clinical Use:** Labor induction/augmentation and postpartum hemorrhage control.
- **Adverse Effects:** Uterine rupture (maternal complication), fetal distress, and water intoxication/hyponatremia (due to its antidiuretic effect).

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Explain the role of Bromocriptine in managing hyperprolactinemia and identify one major psychiatric contraindication.
back:
Mechanism: Dopamine D2 receptor agonist that inhibits prolactin secretion.
- **Clinical Use:** Restores fertility in prolactinomas and acromegaly.
- **Contraindication:** Psychotic illness (e.g., schizophrenia), as D2 agonism can exacerbate symptoms.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Contrast the hormonal composition and clinical derivation of Urofollitropin versus Menotropins (hMG).
back:
- **Urofollitropin:** Purified FSH only; extracted from postmenopausal urine.
- **Menotropins (hMG):** Mixture of FSH and LH; also extracted from postmenopausal urine.
- **Use:** Both treat infertility by stimulating follicle development/spermatogenesis.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Enumerate the androgenic side effects observed in women taking Danazol for endometriosis.
back:
- **Adverse Effects:** Acne, hirsutism, deepening of voice, and weight gain.
- **Mechanism:** Weak partial agonist of androgen receptors.
- **Other Risk:** Potential hepatic dysfunction and cytochrome P450 inhibition.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: In postmenopausal women with an intact uterus, estrogen replacement therapy must be combined with a [___] to prevent the development of endometrial carcinoma.
back:
Progestin (e.g., Medroxyprogesterone).
- **Rationale:** Unopposed estrogen causes endometrial hyperplasia.
- **Note:** Estrogen monotherapy is reserved for patients who have undergone a hysterectomy.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: A 10-year-old child being treated with Somatropin for growth deficiency presents with severe headache and papilledema. Which drug-induced complication is most likely?
back:
Pseudotumor cerebri (Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension).
- **Other GH Toxicities:** Slipped capital femoral epiphysis, progression of scoliosis, and hyperglycemia.
- **Prader-Willi Warning:** Increased risk of asphyxia in severely obese patients.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Detail the specific fetal pathologies associated with the maternal use of Diethylstilbestrol (DES) during pregnancy.
back:
- **Female Offspring:** Clear-cell vaginal adenocarcinoma, infertility, and ectopic pregnancy.
- **Drug Class:** Nonsteroidal estrogen agonist.
- **Status:** Historically used to prevent miscarriage; now strictly avoided in pregnancy.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Distinguish between the clinical indications for Somatropin and Mecasermin in pediatric growth disorders.
back:
- **Somatropin:** GH deficiency, Turner syndrome, chronic renal failure, and Prader-Willi syndrome.
- **Mecasermin:** Growth failure specifically due to severe IGF-1 deficiency (e.g., GH receptor mutations) unresponsive to Somatropin.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: List the potential hepatic toxicities associated with the long-term use of 17-alpha-alkylated anabolic steroids like Oxandrolone.
back:
- **Liver Toxicity:** Cholestatic jaundice and hepatocellular carcinoma.
- **Enzymatic Change:** Elevation of AST/ALT.
- **Other Effects:** Virilization in females and gynecomastia/testicular shrinkage in males.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: In children with growth failure unresponsive to Somatropin due to GH receptor mutations, the recombinant IGF-1 analog [___] is used, which carries a significant risk of hypoglycemia.
back:
• Mecasermin
• Mechanism: Recombinant human IGF-1 replacement
• Precaution: Must consume a meal/snack 20 minutes before administration to prevent severe hypoglycemia.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: A woman undergoing infertility treatment develops sudden ovarian enlargement, ascites, and hypovolemia after receiving a mixture of FSH and LH. Identify the likely complication and the drug class responsible.
back:
• Ovarian Hyperstimulation Syndrome (OHSS)
• Causative Drug: Menotropins (hMG)
• Clinical Use: Ovulation induction in anovulatory women unresponsive to simpler treatments.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Detail the mechanism and primary clinical application of Danazol in gynecological practice.
back:
• Mechanism: Weak partial agonist of progestin/androgen receptors; inhibits P450 enzymes in steroid synthesis.
• Clinical Use: Endometriosis and fibrocystic breast disease.
• Major Side Effects: Weight gain, acne, and hirsutism.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Contrast the pharmacological properties and hepatic impact of Ethinyl Estradiol compared to micronized Estradiol when used in hormone therapy.
back:
• Ethinyl Estradiol: Synthetic, high oral bioavailability, high ratio of hepatic to peripheral effects (increases clotting factors).
• Estradiol: Natural, low oral bioavailability due to first-pass metabolism; hepatic effects minimized by transdermal/vaginal routes.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Outline the specific clinical role and receptor target of Human Chorionic Gonadotropin (hCG) in assisted reproductive protocols.
back:
• Target: LH receptors (identical structure to LH).
• Role: Triggers final oocyte maturation and ovulation.
• Use in Males: Stimulates testicular androgen production in hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: The nonapeptide antagonist [___] is used in various countries as a tocolytic to suppress preterm labor by blocking uterine contraction receptors.
back:
• Atosiban
• Mechanism: Oxytocin receptor antagonist.
• Note: Not FDA approved but used internationally to delay premature delivery.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: A 24-year-old female with PCOS-associated hirsutism is treated with a potassium-sparing diuretic. Explain why this drug is effective for her skin condition.
back:
• Drug: Spironolactone.
• Mechanism: Competitively inhibits androgen receptors and reduces steroid synthesis.
• Adverse Effect: Can cause hyperkalemia and gynecomastia (in males).

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: In patients with metastatic prostate cancer resistant to standard antiandrogens, describe how Ketoconazole provides therapeutic benefit.
back:
• Mechanism: Non-selective inhibition of cytochrome P450 enzymes (including 17,20-lyase).
• Effect: Rapidly suppresses both adrenal and gonadal androgen synthesis.
• Toxicity: Hepatotoxicity and many drug-drug interactions.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Distinguish between Conivaptan and Tolvaptan regarding receptor selectivity and route of administration.
back:
• Conivaptan: Mixed V1a and V2 antagonist; administered via IV infusion.
• Tolvaptan: Selective V2 antagonist; administered orally.
• Monitoring: Tolvaptan use is limited to 30 days due to potential hepatotoxicity.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Enumerate the characteristic hepatic and endocrine adverse effects seen in males abusing high doses of Anabolic Steroids (e.g., Stanozolol).
back:
• Hepatic: Cholestatic jaundice and elevated liver enzymes.
• Endocrine: Testicular shrinkage, azoospermia, and gynecomastia (via feedback inhibition and conversion to estrogen).
• Other: Increased risk of hepatocellular carcinoma.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: A serious adverse effect of Somatropin therapy in children that manifests as headache, nausea, and papilledema is [___].
back:
• Pseudotumor cerebri (idiopathic intracranial hypertension).
• Other high-yield pediatric toxicities include slipped capital femoral epiphysis and progression of scoliosis.
• Adults more commonly experience peripheral edema and myalgia.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: A 50-year-old male treated with Octreotide for acromegaly develops right upper quadrant pain after meals. Explain the pharmacological basis for this finding.
back:
• Somatostatin analogs inhibit gallbladder contractility and reduce bile secretion.
• This leads to the formation of gallstones (cholelithiasis).
• Other side effects include bradycardia and gastrointestinal disturbances.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Explain the specific physiological role of Human Chorionic Gonadotropin (hCG) in female infertility treatment protocols.
back:
• Functions as an LH receptor agonist due to structural similarity.
• Triggers the final stage of oocyte maturation.
• Induces ovulation after follicular development has been stimulated by FSH.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Contrast the clinical risk of endometrial carcinoma between Tamoxifen and Raloxifene when used for postmenopausal prophylaxis.
back:
• Tamoxifen: Partial agonist at the endometrium; significantly increases risk of hyperplasia and cancer.
• Raloxifene: Estrogen antagonist at the endometrium; carries no increased risk of endometrial cancer.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Identify the primary clinical uses of Finasteride and its most common patient-reported sexual adverse effects.
back:
• Clinical Uses: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH) and male-pattern hair loss (alopecia).
• Adverse Effects: Impotence, decreased libido, and rarely gynecomastia.
• It acts by inhibiting 5-alpha-reductase.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Beyond its antidiuretic effect, Desmopressin is indicated for [___] because it increases plasma levels of Factor VIII.
back:
• Mild Hemophilia A and von Willebrand Disease.
• It stimulates extrarenal V2-like receptors to release von Willebrand factor and Factor VIII from endothelial storage sites.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: A woman using Mifepristone and Misoprostol for medical abortion presents with rapid-onset sepsis without fever. This is a rare, fatal complication associated with [___].
back:
• Clostridium sordellii infection.
• Characterized by severe sepsis, leukocytosis, and capillary leak syndrome.
• Misoprostol-specific side effects include significant GI cramping and diarrhea.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: How is Flutamide utilized during the initiation phase of Leuprolide therapy for metastatic prostate cancer?
back:
• Administered during the first week to prevent "tumor flare."
• Competitively blocks androgen receptors to counteract the initial GnRH agonist-induced surge in testosterone.
• Prevents acute worsening of bone pain or urinary obstruction.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Contrast the long-term metabolic effects of Aromatase Inhibitors (e.g., Anastrozole) versus Estrogen on bone mineral density.
back:
• Estrogens: Agonists in bone that reduce resorption and protect against osteoporosis.
• Aromatase Inhibitors: Exhaust estrogen levels, leading to significantly reduced bone density and increased fracture risk.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: List two primary intravenous indications for Oxytocin and its most life-threatening maternal adverse effect.
back:
• Indications: Induction/augmentation of labor and control of postpartum hemorrhage.
• Major Toxicity: Uterine rupture.
• High doses can also cause water intoxication/hyponatremia due to ADH-like activity.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: To provide both FSH and LH activity for stimulating spermatogenesis in hypogonadal men, [___] is extracted from the urine of postmenopausal women.
back:
Menotropins (hMG)
- Contains a mixture of FSH and LH.
- Used for infertility induction in both sexes.
- Sourced from postmenopausal urine due to high levels following cessation of ovarian feedback.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: A 35-year-old male bodybuilder presents with jaundice and right upper quadrant pain. Imaging reveals a hepatic mass. He admits to long-term use of oxandrolone. This presentation is most likely due to [___].
back:
Hepatocellular carcinoma (or Cholestatic jaundice)
- High-dose anabolic steroids are linked to liver toxicity.
- Causes include cholestasis and elevated transaminases.
- 17-alkylated androgens carry the highest risk of hepatic dysfunction.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Explain the mechanism by which Danazol treats endometriosis and describe its primary hormonal receptor profile.
back:
- Inhibits several cytochrome P450 enzymes involved in gonadal steroid synthesis.
- Acts as a weak partial agonist of progestin, androgen, and glucocorticoid receptors.
- Effectively suppresses the midcycle LH and FSH surge.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: A patient with acromegaly requires pharmacotherapy. Contrast the clinical effects of Octreotide with those of Pegvisomant regarding the pituitary tumor itself.
back:
- Octreotide: Somatostatin analog; inhibits GH release and can reduce pituitary tumor size.
- Pegvisomant: GH receptor antagonist; blocks peripheral GH action but does not reduce tumor size or GH secretion.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: List two specific orthopedic and one neurological adverse effect unique to pediatric Somatropin therapy.
back:
- Orthopedic: Slipped capital femoral epiphysis (SCFE) and progression of scoliosis.
- Neurological: Pseudotumor cerebri (idiopathic intracranial hypertension).
- Metabolic: Edema and hyperglycemia.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: The nonapeptide antagonist used as a tocolytic to suppress preterm labor by blocking uterine contractions is [___].
back:
Atosiban
- Antagonist of the oxytocin receptor.
- Not FDA approved but used internationally for preterm labor.
- Prevents oxytocin-stimulated uterine contraction.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: A 28-year-old woman with hirsutism is prescribed Spironolactone. Describe the secondary mechanism (beyond its diuretic effect) that justifies its use in this condition.
back:
- Competitively inhibits androgen receptors in target tissues.
- Weakly inhibits steroid synthesis enzymes.
- Reduces the clinical effects of excess testosterone and DHT on hair follicles.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Detail the pharmacological management required to prevent 'Tumor Flare' during the initiation of GnRH agonist therapy for advanced prostate cancer.
back:
- Administer an androgen receptor antagonist (e.g., Flutamide) during the first week.
- Blocks the initial surge in testosterone synthesis.
- Prevents temporary exacerbation of the malignancy before receptor downregulation occurs.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Distinguish between the tissue-specific mechanism of Fulvestrant and that of Selective Estrogen Receptor Modulators (SERMs).
back:
- Fulvestrant: A pure estrogen receptor antagonist in all tissues.
- SERMs: Mixed agonists/antagonists depending on the tissue (e.g., antagonist in breast, agonist in bone).
- Fulvestrant is used for tamoxifen-resistant breast cancer.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Identify the primary adverse effect of Mecasermin and the recommended clinical strategy to prevent its occurrence.
back:
- Adverse Effect: Hypoglycemia.
- Prevention: Consumption of a snack or meal shortly before or after administration.
- Use: Children with IGF-1 deficiency unresponsive to GH.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: In children being treated with Somatropin for growth hormone deficiency, a rare but serious adverse effect involving increased intracranial pressure is [___].
back: Pseudotumor cerebri (idiopathic intracranial hypertension). Other childhood toxicities include: Slipped capital femoral epiphysis, progression of scoliosis, and peripheral edema.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: A 50-year-old male with acromegaly receives high-dose Bromocriptine. He subsequently develops cold-induced digital vasospasm and pulmonary infiltrates. Identify the underlying drug class.
back: Dopamine D2 receptor agonists. High doses of these ergot derivatives can cause: Peripheral vasospasm, pulmonary infiltrates, and psychiatric disturbances.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Explain the primary clinical mechanism of Oxytocin in the management of postpartum hemorrhage.
back: Activation of G-protein coupled oxytocin receptors on uterine smooth muscle. This induces rhythmic contractions that compress intramyometrial blood vessels, effectively controlling bleeding after delivery.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Contrast the risk of endometrial cancer between postmenopausal women taking unopposed Estrogen versus those taking a combined Estrogen-Progestin regimen.
back: Unopposed Estrogen: High risk of endometrial hyperplasia and adenocarcinoma. Combined Regimen: The progestin component antagonizes the proliferative effect of estrogen on the endometrium, preventing cancer.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Identify the specific organ system that must be monitored via laboratory testing in patients receiving Pegvisomant for acromegaly.
back: The liver (Hepatic system). Pegvisomant is associated with elevated liver enzymes (transaminases), requiring periodic Liver Function Tests (LFTs) to monitor for potential hepatotoxicity.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Menotropins (hMG), extracted from the urine of postmenopausal women, is clinically used to provide both [___] and [___] activity for infertility treatment.
back: FSH (Follicle-Stimulating Hormone) and LH (Luteinizing Hormone). These are used to drive follicle development in women and stimulate spermatogenesis in hypogonadal men.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: A 26-year-old female experiences fatal sepsis due to Clostridium sordellii following a medical abortion. Which drug in the abortifacient regimen is rarely associated with this specific atypical infection?
back: Mifepristone. Common side effects include: Vaginal bleeding and GI distress (nausea/vomiting/diarrhea). Serious but rare complications include sepsis and incomplete abortion.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Explain why Finasteride has a lower risk of causing impotence and loss of libido compared to non-selective androgen receptor antagonists like Flutamide.
back: Finasteride selectively inhibits 5-alpha-reductase, blocking DHT production in specific tissues. It does not interfere with the action of systemic testosterone, which maintains male libido.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Contrast the primary clinical application and major adverse effect of Danazol with those of SERMs like Tamoxifen.
back: Danazol: Used for endometriosis; causes virilization (acne, hirsutism). Tamoxifen: Used for breast cancer; causes hot flushes, thromboembolism, and potential endometrial hyperplasia.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: List two serious fetal complications associated with the excessive administration of Oxytocin during labor induction.
back: Fetal distress (due to uterine ischemia) and placental abruption. In the mother, it may also lead to uterine rupture or water intoxication/hyponatremia.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: The primary metabolic adverse effect of Mecasermin (recombinant IGF-1) that requires the patient to consume a snack or meal shortly before administration is [___].
back: • Hypoglycemia (primary acute risk) • Requires pre-administration caloric intake to prevent glucose drops.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: A 30-year-old female with endometriosis is treated with a drug that causes acne, hirsutism, and weight gain. Identify the likely medication.
back: • Danazol • Acts as a weak partial agonist of progestin and androgen receptors • Inhibits cytochrome P450 enzymes involved in steroid synthesis.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Explain the physiological role of Human Chorionic Gonadotropin (hCG) when used in the treatment of male hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.
back: • Acts as an LH receptor agonist • Stimulates Leydig cells to produce testosterone • Supports spermatogenesis in conjunction with FSH.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: A patient presents with both central diabetes insipidus and bleeding esophageal varices. Contrast the receptor selectivity of the drugs used for these two conditions.
back: • Desmopressin: Selective V2 agonist (treats diabetes insipidus) • Vasopressin: Non-selective V1 and V2 agonist (V1 activation treats variceal bleeding).

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Explain why high doses of exogenous anabolic steroids can paradoxically lead to gynecomastia and testicular shrinkage in men.
back: • Peripheral conversion of excess androgens to estrogens • Feedback inhibition of pituitary LH and FSH release • Results in Leydig cell and testicular atrophy.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: The gonadotropin preparation purified from the urine of postmenopausal women, containing both FSH and LH activity, is [___].
back: • Menotropins (human Menopausal Gonadotropin or hMG).

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: A daughter of a woman who received Diethylstilbestrol (DES) during pregnancy is undergoing a reproductive health screening. Identify her primary risks.
back: • Vaginal clear cell adenocarcinoma • Infertility and ectopic pregnancy • Structural uterine abnormalities.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Describe the physiological mechanism by which postmenopausal estrogen replacement therapy (HRT) contributes to the formation of gallstones.
back: • Increases cholesterol secretion into bile • Decreases gallbladder contractility • Results in lithogenic (stone-forming) bile.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Distinguish between the androgenic side effect profiles of older 19-nortestosterone progestins (e.g., Norethindrone) and newer generations (e.g., Norgestimate).
back: • Older: Higher androgenic activity (acne, weight gain, hirsutism) • Newer: Low androgenic activity (preferred for patients with acne).

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Identify the specific organ toxicity that restricts the oral use of the V2 receptor antagonist Tolvaptan to a 30-day maximum treatment duration.
back: • Hepatotoxicity (liver damage).

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: In the management of euvolemic hyponatremia associated with SIADH, the intravenous vasopressin receptor antagonist used to promote free water excretion is [___].
back: Conivaptan. (Note: Tolvaptan is an oral alternative selective for V2 receptors).

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
coreConcept: Vasopressin V1 Activity in Variceal Bleeding
front: A patient with cirrhosis and bleeding esophageal varices receives an intravenous hormone to reduce portal pressure. Explain the pathophysiology of the drug's therapeutic action.
back: Vasopressin activates V1 receptors on vascular smooth muscle, causing direct vasoconstriction of splanchnic vessels to reduce blood flow into the portal system.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Describe the physiological role of Oxytocin in the third stage of labor and its most significant fluid-related adverse effect.
back: Role: Stimulates uterine contraction to control postpartum hemorrhage. Adverse Effect: Water intoxication and hyponatremia due to cross-reactivity with renal V2 (antidiuretic) receptors.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Contrast the clinical indications and primary metabolic toxicities of Mecasermin versus Somatropin.
back: Mecasermin: Used for IGF-1 deficiency (GH-receptor mutations); causes hypoglycemia. Somatropin: Used for GH deficiency; causes hyperglycemia and edema.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Enumerate two clinical indications for Danazol and its characteristic hepatic adverse effect.
back: Indications: Endometriosis and fibrocystic breast disease. Toxicity: Hepatocellular dysfunction/cholestatic jaundice and virilizing effects (acne, hirsutism).

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: The presence of [___] in a severely obese pediatric patient with Prader-Willi syndrome is a strict contraindication for Somatropin therapy due to the risk of fatal asphyxia.
back: Upper airway obstruction or sleep apnea.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: A 28-year-old female athlete presents with amenorrhea, deepening of voice, and clitoral enlargement. Identify the drug class likely being abused and the mechanism of these findings.
back: Anabolic steroids (Androgens); Virilization occurs through the activation of androgen receptors in non-gonadal tissues.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Explain the mechanism of Spironolactone in treating hirsutism and its most dangerous cardiovascular side effect.
back: Mechanism: Competitive antagonist of androgen receptors and inhibitor of steroid synthesis (17α-hydroxylase). Toxicity: Hyperkalemia leading to cardiac arrhythmias.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Contrast the biological goals of administering Oxytocin versus the oxytocin receptor antagonist Atosiban.
back: Oxytocin: Stimulates uterine contractions to induce or augment labor. Atosiban: Inhibits contractions (tocolytic) to suppress preterm labor.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Identify the primary musculoskeletal toxicity associated with long-term Anastrozole therapy in breast cancer patients.
back: Decreased bone mineral density (osteoporosis) and increased risk of fractures due to the total suppression of estrogen synthesis.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: For children with growth failure unresponsive to Somatropin due to GH receptor mutations (GH insensitivity), the drug of choice is [___].
back:
Mecasermin (recombinant IGF-1).

• Clinical Use: IGF-1 deficiency (Laron dwarfism).
• Key AE: Hypoglycemia (prevented by eating before dosing);
• Potential intracranial hypertension.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: An infertile woman is prescribed a preparation purified from the urine of postmenopausal women containing equal FSH and LH activity. Identify this agent and its primary use.
back:
Menotropins (hMG).

• Clinical Use: Controlled ovarian hyperstimulation/ovulation induction.
• AE: Multiple pregnancies;
• Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS).

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Explain the specific mechanism of Exemestane and identify the patient population for which it is indicated.
back:
Irreversible Aromatase Inhibitor.

• MOA: Suicide inhibition of aromatase, blocking the final step of estrogen synthesis.
• Clinical Use: Hormone-responsive breast cancer in postmenopausal women.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Contrast the primary contraceptive mechanism of progestin-only pills ('mini-pills') with that of combination oral contraceptives.
back:
Progestin-only vs. Combined OCPs:

• Progestin-only: Primarily thickens cervical mucus (blocks sperm) and thins endometrium.
• Combined OCP: Primarily inhibits ovulation by suppressing GnRH/LH/FSH.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Describe the therapeutic role and receptor-level mechanism of Atosiban in obstetrics.
back:
Tocolytic Agent.

• MOA: Oxytocin receptor antagonist.
• Clinical Use: Suppression of preterm labor.
• Note: Not FDA approved but used internationally.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: The weak androgenic steroid used for endometriosis that is notorious for causing acne, hirsutism, and inhibiting multiple Cytochrome P450 enzymes is [___].
back:
Danazol.

• MOA: Partial agonist of androgen/progestin receptors.
• AE: Weight gain; virilization (deep voice); hepatic dysfunction;
• Inhibits P450 enzymes.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: A 17-year-old male with delayed puberty and low testosterone is started on Testosterone Cypionate. What are the long-term metabolic and skeletal risks of this therapy?
back:
Androgen Replacement Risks:

• Skeletal: Premature epiphyseal closure (short stature).
• Metabolic: Cholestatic jaundice; decreased HDL;
• Paradoxical feminization (gynecomastia) if converted to estrogen.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: How does the receptor selectivity and treatment duration limit of Tolvaptan differ from Conivaptan?
back:
Selective V2 Antagonism.

• Selectivity: Tolvaptan (V2 only) vs. Conivaptan (V1a/V2).
• Limitation: Tolvaptan restricted to 30 days due to hepatotoxicity risk.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Distinguish between Bicalutamide and Flutamide regarding their adverse effect profiles in prostate cancer management.
back:
Nonsteroidal Antiandrogens:

• Flutamide: High risk of hepatotoxicity; frequent dosing.
• Bicalutamide: Lower risk of hepatotoxicity; once-daily dosing;
• Both used to prevent GnRH-agonist 'flare'.

category: Enumerate their clinical uses and potential adverse effects
front: Identify the primary clinical indication for Choriogonadotropin alfa and its hormonal mechanism of action.
back:
Recombinant hCG (LH Analog).

• MOA: Activates LH receptors to simulate the natural LH surge.
• Clinical Use: Initiation of final oocyte maturation and ovulation induction.
